newsitem.title: USA: OMB's Raines hopes for budget process culmination.
newsitem.headline: OMB's Raines hopes for budget process culmination.

text.p: Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines said he hoped the round of budget talks beginning Tuesday and scheduled to continue over the next two weeks would lead to the "culmination" of the current budget process.

Speaking to reporters after a speech, Raines said the White House would honour its proposal for $100 billion in savings from the Medicare health care programme for the elderly over the next five years.
On Tuesday the White House team including Raines opened budget negotiations with the Republican chairman of the congressional budget committees as well as their ranking Democratic members.
"We are going to try to kick off what we hope will be the culmination of negotiations regarding the budget not just for 1998 (but for) five years," Raines said in the speech.

Speaking to reporters later, Raines noted that the Congressional Budget Office had scored Clinton's Medicare savings proposal at $82 billion over five years, and said the administration would honour its plan for $100 billion in savings.

Asked if this meant the administration would offer $100 billion as scored by the CBO, Raines said: "Let me just leave it at we're prepared to make good on our $100 billion commitment." Raines also said that the administration would like to see more proposals from the Republican side on this and other matters.
